claims.text: Current EAM references do not adequately represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
A machine-learning model can be trained on ab initio simulations to generate or predict atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning model will capture complex atomic interactions and configurations.
The machine-learning model will represent atomic configurations more accurately than current EAM references.
More accurate representation of atomic configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning model will enhance the predictive capability of EAM potentials.
The intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 20–30% relative to current EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The applicable temperature range is near the alloys' melting points.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing at least five different elements.
The magnitude of path-mismatch reduction may vary with alloy system and machine-learning model.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
